newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS-Battle for position begins in Norway banking.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Battle for position begins in Norway banking.

text.p: Two Norwegian banks squared up on Friday for a battle to take over one of the country's leading mortgage lenders which could spark off a long-expected restructuring of the country's crowded banking sector.

Top commercial bank Den norske Bank ASA (DnB) launched a bid for Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank), just three days after Norway's fourth largest bank, Fokus Bank ASA, proposed a merger with the niche group.
Investors reacted swiftly to the prospect of a bidding war, with BNbank shares jumping almost five percent to 203 crowns on the Oslo bourse by 1400 GMT in heavy turnover of 150 million crowns.

"This involves three companies in the financial sector, two of which are possible takeover candidates. This is the start of the structural changes in Norway's banking sector that we have been waiting for for two years," said an Oslo-based analyst.
DnB said it would offer a cash payment of 184.50 crowns per share, plus BNbank's 1996 dividend of 10.50 crowns.
"The total value of BNbank is thus stipulated at NOK 1,902 million," DnB said in a statement.
On Tuesday, Trondheim-based Fokus Bank proposed an exchange ratio of 3.3 Fokus shares for each share in BNbank, with 20 percent of the consideration paid in cash.
Based on Fokus' closing share price on Monday of 58.50 crowns, the exchange ratio equalled a price on BNbank of 179.85 crowns per share and 10 crowns in dividend, Fokus said.
Fokus told Reuters after learning of DnB's counterbid that it planned to revise its bid. Its merger with BNbank would form a company with total assets of 60 billion crowns.
DnB currently owns 7.4 percent of BNbank shares, and an additional 0.9 percent is held by its insurance subsidiary Vital Forsikring.

"Through the purchase of BNbank, DnB wishes to strengthen Trondheim as a centre of expertise as part of a major effort directed towards customers in the Troendelag region, and at the same time enhance DnB's position in the market for long-term morgage loans to the business sector," DnB's statement said.

Analysts said a counterbid had been expected. Fokus, which is the fruit of a series of fusions between several banks in the late 1980s, is itself regarded as a likely acquisition target in Norway's crowded banking sector.

"There has been a lot of turnover in Fokus lately, maybe 20 percent of the bank has traded in the last two weeks. I wouldn't be surprised if suddenly there was a bid on Fokus itself," another analyst said.

They said DnB's strategy could be based on preventing Fokus from becoming a stronger player while still being vulnerable to a takeover by a larger maybe overseas bank -- such as Sweden's Handelsbanken or Den Danske Bank -- which could result in tougher competition.

If Fokus is successful, it would also strengthen its regional position. This, with Norwegian politics strongly focused on regions, would mean it would be poltically difficult for a larger institution to make a future bid for Fokus, they said.
"DnB sees much strategic value in blocking Fokus, both in a business and political sense. It makes sense to keep Fokus as small as possible," commented another market source.
Most agree DnB is likely to be the successful bidder, although they expect Fokus to raise its exchange ratio and for DnB to subsequently raise its cash offer before the battle was settled.

"DnB has got much more muscle than Fokus. Shareholders prefer cash offers and the board at BNbank would probably prefer DnB," said another analyst. "But I expect a bidding war and in the end it will be BNbank shareholders who come out on top."
